proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof ("deleting any point of a representation would give a competitor of smaller mass; hence T = 0, Θ :≡ 0 works and (2) is vacuous"), with the details supplied. Uses the sibling mass_eq_measure (M_W(Y) = μ_R(W) for open W ⊆ U and any representation R of Y). Facts: μHE[0] = μH[0] (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) is the counting measure (μH[0]{p} = 1, Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton), so a set is μHE[0]-null iff it is empty.
1. T is integer multiplicity (first component of IsMinimizingIn); let R = (M, θ, ξ) represent it. Because μHE[0]-null sets are empty, the field `orients` holds at every point of M.
2. Local finiteness: for compact K ⊆ U, #(M ∩ K) ≤ Σ_{q∈M∩K} θ(q) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ < ∞ (θ ≥ 1 on M), so M ∩ K is finite.
3. Suppose M ≠ ∅ and fix p ∈ M. Choose r₀ > 0 with closedBall(p, r₀) ⊆ U; M ∩ closedBall(p, r₀) is finite by step 2, so there is r ∈ (0, r₀] with M ∩ closedBall(p, r) = {p}. Put W := ball(p, r): W is open and closure W ⊆ closedBall(p, r) is compact and contained in U.
4. By mass_eq_measure, M_W(T) = μ_R(W) = θ(p)·H⁰({p}) = θ(p) ≥ 1.
5. p ∈ spt T. Otherwise p lies in an open set V with compact closure in U on which T vanishes; every admissible form for V ∩ W has tsupport in V, so M_{V∩W}(T) = 0, while by mass_eq_measure M_{V∩W}(T) = μ_R(V ∩ W) ≥ θ(p) ≥ 1 (p ∈ V ∩ W, which is open and ⊆ U). Contradiction. Hence p ∈ spt T ⊆ A.
6. Competitor. Let X ∈ 𝒟_0(U) be X(ω) := θ(p)·ξ(p)(ω(p)) (continuous: convergence in 𝒟⁰(U) implies pointwise convergence) and S := T − X. Then R_S := (M ∖ {p}, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U representing S: M ∖ {p} is Borel, ⊆ U and countably 0-rectifiable (subset of M); measurability, positivity and local integrability are inherited from R; orientation: for x ∈ M ∖ {p} with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M x Q, the blow-ups η_{x,ρ}(M) and η_{x,ρ}(M ∖ {p}) differ only by the point (p − x)/ρ, which leaves every bounded set as ρ ↓ 0 (|p − x| > 0), so for f ∈ C_c the two blow-up integrals coincide for small ρ and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 (M ∖ {p}) x Q holds, with ξ(x) still orienting Q; representation: S(ω) = ∫_M θξ(ω) dH⁰ − θ(p)ξ(p)(ω(p))·H⁰({p}) = ∫_{M∖{p}} θξ(ω) dH⁰. So S is integer multiplicity.
7. Admissibility. S − T = −X as currents, i.e. (S − T)(ω) = −θ(p)ξ(p)(ω(p)). Every q ∈ U ∖ {p} has a ball B with closure compact in U ∖ {p} (U ∖ {p} is open), and forms supported in B vanish at p, so S − T vanishes on B; hence spt(S − T) ⊆ {p}, which is compact and contained in A ∩ W (p ∈ A by step 5, p ∈ W). SameBoundary S T holds trivially for n = 0, W is open and compactly contained in U.
8. Minimality gives M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S). By mass_eq_measure for S and R_S, M_W(S) = μ_{R_S}(W) = Σ_{q ∈ (M∖{p})∩W} θ(q) = 0 since M ∩ W = {p}, whereas M_W(T) = θ(p) ≥ 1 by step 4. Contradiction; therefore M = ∅.
9. With M = ∅, T(ω) = ∫_∅ θξ(ω) = 0 for every ω, so T = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). Then spt T = ∅: every y ∈ U has r > 0 with closedBall(y, r) ⊆ U (U open), ball(y, r) has compact closure in U and the zero current vanishes on it, so y lies in the zero region. Finally, for every W, M_W(T) is the supremum of ofReal T(ω) = ofReal 0 = 0 over a set containing the zero form, hence M_W(T) = 0.
key_steps: A 0-dimensional integer multiplicity current is a locally finite sum of signed point masses with integer weights θ ≥ 1.
Every carrier point p lies in spt T ⊆ A, because the mass of T near p is at least θ(p) (mass_eq_measure).
Deleting p gives an integer multiplicity competitor S with spt(S − T) = {p} and M_W(S) = 0 < θ(p) ≤ M_W(T), contradicting minimality; so the carrier is empty and T = 0.
